summary: aiosendletter 3.9 archives local app data and uploads it to an author-controlled Cloudflare Worker after attempting UAC elevation
details: The package defines an init() routine that, on Windows, calls ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb to relaunch the current Python interpreter elevated, then uses shutil.make_archive to zip a directory under %LOCALAPPDATA% and POSTs the resulting archive as a multipart 'document' upload to the hardcoded endpoint https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/. The destination is a Cloudflare Workers host unrelated to any declared publisher or purpose, and the upload is unconditional — the installer does not configure it. pyproject.toml additionally declares `ctypes` as a runtime dependency; because `ctypes` is a Python standard-library module, pip resolves that name against PyPI and installs whichever package currently holds it, unpinned, running its install-time code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
